school.name: Egypt Photonics Seasonal School
school.tagline: Intensive technical immersion bridging classroom physics with modern photonic design.
school.description: A premier five-day national training school rotating among Egyptian universities. Featuring theoretical foundations, computational simulation bootcamps, and physical device characterization led by university faculty, industry leaders, and international Optica traveling lecturers.
school.hostInstitution: Ain Shams University and The American University in Cairo (AUC)
school.location: Cairo, Egypt (In-person with hybrid broadcast to Alexandria and Upper Egypt campuses)
school.format: Five-Day Intensive Course with Daily Hands-on Computer Laboratories
school.eligibility: Undergraduate seniors, graduate researchers (M.Sc. and Ph.D.), and junior industry engineers.
school.certificate: Official Certificate of Completion awarded jointly by Optica Egypt and host institutions.
school.tuition: Subsidized by Optica Global and industry sponsors; free admission for selected scholarship fellows.

modules.title: Integrated Silicon and Silicon Nitride Photonics
modules.description: Electromagnetic waveguide theory, passive components, grating couplers, ring resonators, Mach-Zehnder interferometers, and multi-mode interferometers (MMI).
modules.instructor: Faculty and Research Fellows in Integrated Optics

modules.title: Photonic Design Automation and Scripted Layout
modules.description: Python-first layout workflows, parameterized cells (PCells), DRC verification, waveguide routing, and GDSII export using gdsfactory.

modules.title: Computational Electrodynamics and Numerical Modeling
modules.description: Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) fundamentals, boundary conditions (PML), frequency-domain eigenmode solving, and S-parameter extraction with Meep.
modules.instructor: Computational Modeling Faculty and Simulation Specialists

modules.title: Optical MEMS, Sensors, and Applied Spectroscopy
modules.description: Microsystems engineering, MEMS FTIR spectroscopy, photonic crystal refractive index sensors, bio-photonics, and industrial gas detection.
modules.instructor: Prof. Diaa Khalil and Prof. Yasser Sabry (Ain Shams University / Si-Ware Systems)

modules.title: Quantum Photonics and Nonlinear Optical Physics
modules.description: Single-photon sources, spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC), quantum entanglement on chip, and nonlinear Kerr optical phenomena.
modules.instructor: Assoc. Prof. Salem Hegazy (Cairo University / Zewail City)

highlights.title: Daily 3-Hour Hands-on CAD Lab
highlights.description: Every participant works through verified Jupyter notebook exercises, implementing real layout designs and running electromagnetic simulations.

highlights.title: Traveling Lecturer Masterclass
highlights.description: Direct in-person sessions delivered by international Optica Traveling Lecturers sponsored by the Optica Foundation.

highlights.title: Industry Career Colloquium
highlights.description: Exclusive networking panels with Egyptian photonics companies, fabless start-ups, and international graduate scholarship advisors.

webinars.title: Distinguished Webinar Series
webinars.description: Regular virtual technical lectures connecting Egyptian students and researchers with leading international scientists, Optica traveling lecturers, and Egyptian photonics leaders across the global diaspora.
features: Live interactive Q and A with global researchers
Open-access digital video archive with downloadable slides
Attendance certificates for verified student participants
Special sessions on graduate admissions and fellowship applications

schedule.title: Advances in Silicon Photonic Transceivers and Optical Computing for AI Data Centers
schedule.speaker: Prof. Mohamed A. Swillam
schedule.role: Professor and Chair of Physics, The American University in Cairo (AUC)
schedule.abstract: Explores how high-density integrated silicon photonics addresses the interconnect bottleneck in modern artificial intelligence clusters, examining co-packaged optics, micro-ring modulators, and neural optical accelerators.

schedule.title: Open-Source EDA and Design Automation for Next-Generation Integrated Photonics
schedule.speaker: Dr. Mehdi Saligane
schedule.role: Research Scientist, University of Michigan; Chair, IEEE SSCS TC-OSE
schedule.abstract: An overview of how open-source silicon tools (gdsfactory, KLayout, OpenLane) are revolutionizing hardware accessibility, drawing parallels between open-silicon and open-photonics ecosystems.

schedule.title: Miniaturized Optical MEMS FTIR Spectrometers: From Egyptian Lab to Global Commercialization
schedule.speaker: Prof. Diaa Khalil
schedule.role: Professor of Photonics, Ain Shams University; Chief Scientist, Si-Ware Systems
schedule.abstract: The journey of conceiving, fabricating, and commercializing the NeoSpectra handheld FTIR spectrometer, demonstrating the immense economic and scientific potential of Egyptian deep-tech innovation.

contests.title: Hands-on Contests and Student Challenges
contests.description: Learning reaches its highest impact when tested in competition. Optica Egypt provides structured challenges where classroom theory translates into working open-source code and fabricated silicon.

items.title: Software-Defined Photonics Hackathon
items.category: Software Tools and AI Models Championship
items.description: A seven-week nationwide build sprint challenging teams to create Python automation scripts, FDTD pre-processing tools, and deep learning inverse design surrogates.

items.title: Egypt Photonic Chipathon
items.description: Annual layout design contest where university teams submit DRC-clean photonic integrated circuit designs for subsidized multi-project wafer (MPW) fabrication.

items.title: Optica Egypt Student Paper and Poster Competition
items.description: Annual academic symposium contest celebrating outstanding undergraduate capstone projects and graduate research across optics, photonics, and laser engineering.
